grammar_notes.text: Reduplication is used for emphasis on a word being heavy or more of something. Example: Yupyupseunne (heavily wooded river) and Wawawa (heavy snow).
grammar_notes.source_excerpt: Reduplication- if a word shows reduplication then it is for emphasis on it being heavy or more of… Ie: Yupyupseunne= (yup=wood, seunne=river) heavily wooded river Wawawa= snow- heavily

grammar_notes.text: 2nd person singular possessive prefix is 'ya-' or 'yi-', and 3rd person possessive suffix is 'wa'.
grammar_notes.source_excerpt: 2nd person singular possessive= ya-/yi- 3rd person possessive= wa

pronunciation_notes.text: a= ah as in Father, ą́= (no pronunciation given), e=ay as in way, i=ee as in weep, o=oh as in Row, oo= elongated oh, u= oo as in choose
pronunciation_notes.source_excerpt: Pronunciation: a= ah as in Father ą́= e=ay as in way i=ee as in weep o=oh as in Row oo= elongated oh u= oo as in choose

pronunciation_notes.text: r&n are nasalized and trilled (probably not the right word), č=ch, J= ch
pronunciation_notes.source_excerpt: Pronunciation: r&n are nasalized and trilled (probably not the right word) č=ch J= ch

pronunciation_notes.text: Glottal stop is represented as a pause between uh and oh in 'uhoh', written as uh--oh.
pronunciation_notes.source_excerpt: Pronunciation: Glottal stop- the pause between uh and oh in uhoh represented as= uh--oh

pronunciation_notes.text: Wa cahn- oo= u, o= ah, che= chi, Oh, ou= oo, au= aw, e=eh
